first_run.label: Welcome to MathTrail
first_run.lead: MathTrail gives a child olympiad-style maths tasks for grades 1 to 6, right here in the chat, and goes through every mistake. An adult sets it up: a parent or a tutor.
first_run.pseudonym: The child is known by a pseudonym alone: never a real name, a birth date or a school.
first_run.fill: A pseudonym and the grade, 1 to 6. If you like, also the child's interests, what they have not met at school yet, and the language of the lessons.
first_run.data: In one file in your own Google Drive, which you can open, download or delete. MathTrail keeps nothing on its side.
first_run.start: Ask in this chat for a MathTrail profile, and answer what it asks. You can change it later, under Profile & progress.
card.unreadable: This card can't be shown here. The chat says the same in words.
trap.off_by_one: Off by one when counting gaps
trap.reversed_relation: Mixed up more and less, before and after
trap.best_case_not_worst: Counted on luck instead of the worst case
trap.trusted_statement: Believed a statement without checking it
trap.number_from_text: Took a number from the question as the answer
trap.percent_wrong_base: Took the percentage of the wrong amount
trap.part_whole_swap: Mixed up the part and the whole
trap.ratio_total_confusion: Mixed up the parts of a ratio and the total
trap.remainder_vs_quotient: Mixed up the quotient and the remainder
trap.first_move_assumed: Assumed the first move always wins
advice.off_by_one: Before answering, draw a quick sketch: the posts as dots and the gaps between them, then count both.
advice.missed_case: List the cases in a fixed order, smallest first, and tick each one off so that none is left out.
advice.double_count: Write each option down once, in a fixed order, and look for repeats before counting them.
advice.ignored_not: Read the question aloud and circle the word “not” before solving it.
advice.answered_other_question: Before answering, say in your own words what the question asks for, and check the answer against it.
advice.stopped_early: After each step, ask whether that is what the question wants, or only a step towards it.
advice.wrong_operation: Act the story out with small objects or a drawing to see whether things are added, taken away or shared.
advice.reversed_relation: Draw the comparison as a line from the smallest to the largest before reading off the answer.
advice.best_case_not_worst: Ask what the unluckiest possible way would be, and make sure the answer holds even then.
advice.trusted_statement: For each speaker, try both: what follows if they tell the truth, and what follows if they lie.
advice.time_unit_mixup: Draw a clock face and count on in minutes, remembering that an hour has 60 of them, not 100.
advice.number_from_text: Before writing a number down, say which calculation it comes from: a number copied from the question is rarely the answer.
advice.wrong_parity: Check parity on small numbers first, such as 1 + 3 and 3 + 5, then say the rule out loud.
advice.ignored_condition: Reread the question and mark every condition, such as “different” or “exactly once”, then check the answer against each.
advice.percent_wrong_base: Ask first: a percentage of what? Write that whole amount down before taking the percentage.
advice.part_whole_swap: Draw the whole as a bar and shade the part, then check which of the two the question asks for.
advice.ratio_total_confusion: Draw the ratio as equal boxes, count all the boxes for the total, then work out what one box holds.
advice.remainder_vs_quotient: Share real objects into groups, then say aloud which number is the groups and which is what is left over.
advice.area_perimeter_swap: Trace the edge with a finger for the perimeter and colour the inside for the area, then reread which one is asked for.
advice.first_move_assumed: Play the game a few times from small positions and see who wins each one before deciding.
